meta.title: Give away a whole clearance in one post
meta.author: edwh

_note: Screenshot scenes position callouts by `ref` (a label measured live by capture into <shot>.boxes.json) and set focusAuto:true, so the renderer derives both the highlight boxes and the zoom from the real element positions — no hand-measured coordinates.

scenes.title: Give away a whole clearance in one post
scenes.subtitle: Offer dozens of items at once — and let people pick exactly what they want.

scenes.heading: A clearance used to mean dozens of posts.
bullets: A charity clearing an office can have 100+ things to rehome.
Today that's one Freegle post per item — each written and photographed by hand.
Replies land scattered across all of them.
scenes.caption: What if the whole clearance were a single, browsable offer?
One post holds the whole clearance — your area, the items, and when people can collect.
Start with your area, then give the whole clearance a name.
Add every item — type them in or paste a spreadsheet — each with its quantity and condition.

callouts.ref: Type them in — or paste a spreadsheet

scenes.caption: Offer set collection times — then post the whole lot in one go.
Recipients see one browsable catalogue — turn on the items you'd like; a stepper sets how many.

callouts.ref: A browsable catalogue in one offer

scenes.caption: Pick a collection time, then one click tells the giver everything you chose.

scenes.heading: It fits in everywhere people already look.
bullets: The clearance turns up in the daily digest email, with photos.
Older views still get a clear, readable list — items and collection times.
Nothing new for people to learn — it's just a richer offer.

scenes.title: What this unlocks
bullets: List a whole clearance as one post.
People pick exactly the items — and how many — they want.
Every request arrives as a single message against the catalogue.
